newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Formosa mulls Australia project - paper.
newsitem.headline: Formosa mulls Australia project - paper.

text.p: Taiwan's Formosa Plastics may build a petrochemical complex in Australia in a bid to meet growing demand for petrochemical raw materials in Asia, a local newspaper reported on Monday.

Formosa, Taiwan's biggest industrial conglomerate, began considering the project after its chairman visited Queensland in 1996 to seek coal imports for his company's petrochemical complex in southern Taiwan, the Economic Daily News reported.
The newspaper said the Australian complex would export petrochemical products to other Asian countries, including China.
Formosa officials declined to comment on the report.

The company in 1992 obtained Taiwan government approval to build a US$9 billion complex, including a naphtha cracker and an oil refinery, in southern Taiwan. Formosa also plans to build a power plant near the complex.
Company officials have said several plants inside the complex would finish construction and begin production in the second half of 1997, although the whole complex would not be completed until 1999.

Formosa recently was forced by the Taiwan government to suspend a US$3 billion power station project in China due to concerns that Taiwan's economy was becoming overdependent on its political arch rival.
But Formosa chairman Wang Yung-ching said the group would not abandon the China project even if it meant waiting for "six months or one year".
